title: Order Items With No Discount Applied
description:
Find all order items that had **no discount applied**. A discount is applied to a specific (order_id, product_id) combination. Return items where no matching discount record exists.

**Table: order_items** — `item_id`, `order_id`, `product_id`, `price`

**Table: discounts** — `discount_id`, `order_id`, `product_id`, `discount_pct`

Output columns: `item_id`, `order_id`, `product_id`, `price`. Order by `item_id`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE order_items (item_id INTEGER, order_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, price DECIMAL(10,2)); CREATE TABLE discounts (discount_id INTEGER, order_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, discount_pct DECIMAL(5,2)); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1,1,101,100.00),(2,1,102,50.00),(3,2,101,100.00),(4,2,103,75.00),(5,3,102,50.00),(6,3,104,120.00),(7,4,101,100.00),(8,4,105,30.00),(9,5,103,75.00),(10,5,106,90.00),(11,6,104,120.00),(12,6,105,30.00); INSERT INTO discounts VALUES (1,1,101,10.00),(2,2,103,5.00),(3,3,102,15.00),(4,4,101,20.00);
solution_sql: SELECT oi.item_id, oi.order_id, oi.product_id, oi.price FROM order_items oi LEFT JOIN discounts d ON oi.order_id = d.order_id AND oi.product_id = d.product_id WHERE d.discount_id IS NULL ORDER BY oi.item_id;

test_cases.description: 4 discounts cover items 1,4,5,7; the remaining 8 items have no discount

hints: Use a LEFT JOIN from order_items to discounts on BOTH order_id AND product_id.
After the LEFT JOIN, rows with no matching discount will have NULL in all discount columns.
Filter WHERE d.discount_id IS NULL to keep only the unmatched rows (the anti-join pattern).
explanation: The LEFT JOIN keeps all order_items rows regardless of whether a discount exists. The ON clause matches on both order_id and product_id together. When no discount row matches, the joined discount columns are NULL — filtering WHERE d.discount_id IS NULL isolates items that never received a discount. Items 2, 3, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 have no corresponding discount entry.
